title: Banner Grabbing: Service Identification 🏷️
description: Send and receive data to grab service banners, identifying software versions and potential vulnerabilities.

slides.title: What is a Banner?
slides.content:
# The Welcome Message

Many services, when you connect, send a banner (like SSH sends `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.9p1`). HTTP servers respond with headers. FTP, SMTP, etc., all have banners.

Banner grabbing means connecting to a port and reading whatever the server sends first. This reveals the software and version.

slides.title: Simple Banner Grab (no data sent)
slides.codeSnippet:
import socket

s = socket.socket()
s.settimeout(2)
try:
    s.connect(('example.com', 80))
    banner = s.recv(1024).decode(errors='ignore')
    print(banner)
except:
    print("No banner")
finally:
    s.close()

quizData.question: Why might a banner not appear after a TCP connection?

options.text: The service sends nothing until the client sends a request
All services send a banner immediately

quizData.explanation: Some protocols (like HTTP) wait for a client request; others (SSH, FTP) send a banner immediately.

slides.title: Grabbing HTTP Service Banners
slides.content:
# For HTTP, send a HEAD request

```python
request = b"HEAD / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n"
s.send(request)
response = s.recv(4096)
print(response.decode())
```
This reveals server software in the `Server` header.

slides.title: Identify Web Server Software
slides.codeSnippet:
import socket

s = socket.socket()
s.settimeout(2)
s.connect(('example.com', 80))
s.send(b'HEAD / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n')
resp = s.recv(1024).decode()
for line in resp.split('\r\n'):
    if line.lower().startswith('server:'):
        print(line)
        break
s.close()

quizData.question: FTP servers typically send a banner immediately upon connection.
quizData.explanation: FTP (port 21) usually sends a '220' banner right after connection.

slides.title: Combining Port Scan + Banner Grab
slides.content:
# We can now build a reconnaissance tool

1. Scan a range of ports.
2. For open ports, attempt to grab a banner.
3. Print results.

This is the heart of basic reconnaissance. We'll build a full tool in Chapter 12.

slides.title: Legal Warning ⚖️
slides.content:
## Only scan systems you own or have permission to test.

Scanning random hosts is illegal. Use `scanme.nmap.org` (provided by Nmap for testing) or your own lab.
